components.name: Primary Action Button
components.description: Bold tactile action trigger with hard offset shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 48px; padding: 12px 24px; background-color: #ff5c1a; color: #121410; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; border: 2px solid #121410; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 0 #121410; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #e84a10; box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 0 #121410; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translate(2px, 2px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 #121410; }

narrative.overview:
SMS Guardian combines the tactile confidence of an industrial dispatch terminal with the warm, authoritative legibility of editorial broadsheets. The aesthetic rejects generic sterile corporate SaaS and dark-mode cyberpunk clichés. Instead, it positions message verification as a deliberate, reliable diagnostic tool — physical, grounded, and alert.

The interface lives in a daylight state on warm, unbleached parchment (#f3efe4), anchored by solid 2px ink borders and hard, un-blurred block drop shadows. Against this tactile paper background, high-contrast obsidian console panels (#080a08) host live scanning telemetry, laser sweeps, and luminous signal lights. The resulting atmosphere feels like operating an analog radar console in an intelligence reading room.
keyCharacteristics: Tactile Neo-Brutalism with Restraint: Thick 2px structural ink strokes paired with crisp hard offset drop shadows (4px to 8px), softened by organic corner radiuses (8px to 16px).
Paper & Phosphor Contrast: Warm daytime editorial paper for reading and inputs, juxtaposed against deep void black for machine telemetry and dark-room radar sweeps.
Micro-Telemetry Typographic Hierarchy: Compressed, personality-rich variable display type juxtaposed with ultra-legible utilitarian body copy and disciplined monospace telemetry stamps.

rules.name: The High-Alert Restraint Rule
rules.body: Signal Vermilion (#ff5c1a) must never be used as a general background or decorative flood. It is reserved strictly for singular calls-to-action, scan sweeps, and alert badges. When everything shouts, nothing warns.

rules.name: The Paper-and-Phosphor Rule
rules.body: High-level content, explanation, and form input remain in the warm paper realm (#f3efe4). Real-time automated data streams (the live demo feed, splash boot loader) exist in dark phosphor chambers (#080a08 / #121410).

rules.name: The Telemetry Stamp Rule
rules.body: All timestamps, endpoints, status states, character counts, and index markers must be formatted in uppercase JetBrains Mono with wide tracking (0.14em–0.2em).

rules.name: The Zero-Fuzz Elevation Rule
rules.body: No Gaussian blurred shadows may be used on light card surfaces. Elevation on paper is strictly communicated through solid 2px #121410 outlines and discrete coordinate translations (translate(x, y)).

dos: Do preserve 2px solid ink strokes around primary modules and cards.
Do use uppercase monospace (JetBrains Mono) with wide tracking for telemetry and status labels.
Do provide instant visual feedback on interactive button presses using coordinate translation and shadow collapse.
Do respect user preferences for reduced motion by immediately showing resolved UI states.
donts: Don't use soft, fuzzy CSS box-shadows on daylight parchment cards.
Don't flood large background areas with primary orange (#ff5c1a).
Don't use decorative generic stock photography or illustrative cartoons; maintain the authentic signal intelligence instrument aesthetic.
Don't omit confidence percentages or replace probabilistic machine verdicts with false claims of absolute certainty.
